# input: # `canonical` is the GeoNames id for a place and canonical metres for a
# distance. A bare place formats to its facts — name, currency, calling code,
# zone, abbreviated population (spec §5.3) — and a distance formats as the
# length kind already does, in km.
# A code is read as a code only when it is written as one: "ua" lowercase is a
# word to the matcher (spec §5.1's guard, widened — "and" is Andorra and "ago"
# is Angola), so "japan to UA" is the form that resolves, and the country's name
# is what a lowercase query is expected to carry.
# Rows that are not about places at all. Registering this kind must not cost
# another one its reading: "km" is Comoros as well as a kilometre, and "and" is
# Andorra. The fold is destructive, so a claim here has no second chance.
